request.questionText: The file franchise.csv contains data from 807 respondents to a scientific survey about the Star Wars film franchise, including these variables: SeenFilms: Yes/No indicator for whether respondent has seen any of the Star Wars franchise films ConsiderFan: Yes/No indicator for whether respondent considers themselves a fan of the Star Wars film franchise Gender: indicator for whether respondent identifies as a Female, or else not_Female Age --- in years Income --- annual income in U.S. dollars Education --- level of education (High school, Bachelor, Graduate, etc) Region --- location of residence in U.S. (Mountain, Pacific, New England, etc) A data scientist interested Star Wars fanbase demography wonders about the extent to which age is a factor in whether someone considers themselves to be a fan of the franchise? Are 'Yes' respondents to the ConsiderFan variable significantly older or younger (on average) relative to 'No' respondents to the ConsiderFan variable? Use these variables along with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval (based on 5000 simulations) to fill in the blanks below with the best answer from each dropdown list: Respondents who consider themselves fans are [ Select ] ["older", "younger"] (on average) than non-fans by approximately [ Select ] ["4", "45", "1", "49", "6"] years. The observed age difference is [ Select ] ["not generalizable", "generalizable"] to a broader reference population because the range of plausible values for the true group difference represented by the calculated bootstrap interval [ Select ] ["consists of both positive and negative numbers", "does not contain zero"] . With 95% confidence, individuals who do NOT consider themselves to be Star Wars fans are at least approximately [ Select ] ["2 years", "47 years", "6 years", "1 year", "4 years"] older than those who do consider themselves to be Star Wars fans.
